source: Department of Agricultural Extension (នាយកដ្ឋានផ្សព្វផ្សាយកសិកម្ម), Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries, Cambodia — booklet 'ដំណាំពោត' (Corn Crop), Issue 1, 2003, funded by Asian Development Bank (ADB), Loan/Grant No. 1445-CAM(SF), section III: Botanical characteristics of corn
text:
Corn is a grass-family (Poaceae) annual crop with a growth cycle length that varies by variety, commonly cited as 85, 90, 100, 110, 130, and up to 185 days from planting to harvest. Waxy/glutinous corn varieties specifically have shorter cycles of about 85, 90, and 110 days.

Corn plant height reaches roughly 1.5-3m depending on variety; American-type field corn can reach up to 5m.

Corn has a fibrous root system, plus brace (prop) roots that emerge from the lower stem nodes above the soil surface, which anchor and support the plant and help prevent lodging.

A special characteristic of this crop is that it is monoecious, bearing separate male and female flowers on the same plant: the male flower (tassel) is at the top of the plant, while the female flower (silk/ear) forms in the leaf axil partway down the stalk. The tassel is the source of pollen for the crop.
